cream-50.note: page background and cards. No pure white anywhere in this system.

blush-200.note: PRIMARY CTA fill, and THE offset shape for life

coral-700.note: the ONLY coral for text on light

clay-500.note: brand secondary — the word 'focal'. 2.40:1, never body text

clay-700.note: CORRECTED from #8A7B68 (3.95:1). Muted text — 4.78:1 on cream-50. Not yet corrected in the canvas.

dune-700.note: gold text on the sand/AI surface

ink-line.note: every line, every mark — 8.93:1. NEVER pure black.

ink-scrim.note: photo scrims; also the Night Dive card surface

danger-text.note: danger-700. Error text ON danger-surface #F5DCDC — 5.30:1. Ratified by Design System section 09 (7 Sep 2026), which superseded the interim #B82D2D.

info-text.note: 4.29:1 on info-surface — sub-AA, flagged in docs/FOUNDATION.md, not fixed

shape-water.note: the filled silhouette behind a water mark

shape-life.note: the filled silhouette behind a life/motion mark

shape-land.note: the filled silhouette behind a land/culture mark

focus-ring.note: = lagoon-focus. 2px ring at 2px offset, drawn as the camera-focus ring.

cta-label.note: = ink-900. The primary button label is always this.

danger-text-on-cream.note: Error text on cream-50 — 5.26:1. Section 09: #C13333 was never wrong on cream, it only failed on its own tint. Pick by ground.

c-bg.note: CONSOLE · Daylight. Page ground for the admin console and the operator app. A near-white biased green so it never glares in Dahab sun. Deliberately not cream-50: the two consoles are a separate visual system from the traveller app, chosen 16 Sep 2026 because a dense operational tool and a holiday booking app are not the same product.

c-surface.note: CONSOLE. Panels, rows, sheets and cards.

c-raised.note: CONSOLE. Hover, selected row, secondary button fill, inactive chip.

c-edge.note: CONSOLE. The hairline between rows. A decorative separator, deliberately below 3:1 — it identifies no control, and rules that shout turn a dense table into a grid of boxes.

c-edge-strong.note: CONSOLE. The border of an input, or any boundary that carries meaning — 3.32:1 on c-surface, clearing WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast.

c-muted.note: CONSOLE. Column headers, secondary lines, timestamps — 6.17:1 on c-surface.

c-accent.note: CONSOLE. = lagoon-600, so the console's one colour is already a brand value. It is a FILL, never ink: 4.43:1 on c-bg carries a label but falls short of AA as text. For a coloured word use c-link.

c-on-accent.note: CONSOLE. The label on c-accent — 4.71:1. Off-white, not #FFFFFF, so 'no pure white anywhere' stays true across the whole project. This is the only fill in Dahab Focal that carries a light label; the traveller CTA is still ink on blush.

c-link.note: CONSOLE. Accent-coloured text and links — 5.56:1 on c-bg.

c-focus.note: CONSOLE. Focus ring — 3.75:1 on c-bg. Darker than lagoon-focus, which clears 3:1 against cream but only reaches 2.88 against this ground.

c-ok.note: CONSOLE. Verified, active, balanced — 5.99:1 on c-ok-bg, 6.85:1 on c-surface.

c-warn.note: CONSOLE. Expiring, under review, partly filled — 5.9:1 on c-warn-bg.

c-bad.note: CONSOLE. Expired, suspended, blocked, disputed — 6:1 on c-bad-bg, 7.01:1 on c-surface.

c-info.note: CONSOLE. Applied, pending, informational — 5.6:1 on c-info-bg. Darker than c-accent because this one is read as a word, not used as a fill.

c-area-run.note: CONSOLE · area tint. Run the day — departures, bookings, the calendar. Lagoon, because it is the brand colour and this is the work the brand exists for. Behind a module's icon on Home, and nowhere a status is being reported.

c-area-run-ink.note: CONSOLE · the icon on c-area-run. Clears 4.5:1 on its tint and on c-surface, so it can carry a word if a tile ever needs one.

c-area-supply.note: CONSOLE · area tint. Operators — papers, fleet, staff. Amber, the colour of expiry, which is the theme of the whole vendor model. Behind a module's icon on Home, and nowhere a status is being reported.

c-area-supply-ink.note: CONSOLE · the icon on c-area-supply. Clears 4.5:1 on its tint and on c-surface, so it can carry a word if a tile ever needs one.

c-area-demand.note: CONSOLE · area tint. Catalogue and travellers. Plum — distinct from every status colour, so a demand tile never reads as a warning. Behind a module's icon on Home, and nowhere a status is being reported.

c-area-demand-ink.note: CONSOLE · the icon on c-area-demand. Clears 4.5:1 on its tint and on c-surface, so it can carry a word if a tile ever needs one.

c-area-money.note: CONSOLE · area tint. Money — ledger, payouts, pricing. Green, and deliberately a different green from c-ok so a module is never mistaken for a status. Behind a module's icon on Home, and nowhere a status is being reported.

c-area-money-ink.note: CONSOLE · the icon on c-area-money. Clears 4.5:1 on its tint and on c-surface, so it can carry a word if a tile ever needs one.

c-area-platform.note: CONSOLE · area tint. Platform — access, audit, health. Slate: infrastructure should be the quietest thing on the screen. Behind a module's icon on Home, and nowhere a status is being reported.

c-area-platform-ink.note: CONSOLE · the icon on c-area-platform. Clears 4.5:1 on its tint and on c-surface, so it can carry a word if a tile ever needs one.

c-glass.note: CONSOLE · c-surface at 88% — the floating tab bar, over a backdrop blur. Where blur is unsupported the bar reads as a slightly transparent c-surface, which is still legible because every label on it is c-text or c-link on a near-solid ground.

info-text.note: 9.5:1 on bg, 8.3:1 on surface, 11.3:1 on its own strip.

danger-text-on-cream.note: Danger text directly on the night page ground — 8.2:1 on bg. Pairs with the light #C13333, so StatusPill onCream works in both themes.

c-bg.note: CONSOLE · Daylight after dark. A neutral cool-dark, not Night Dive's warm green-black — the console is its own system in both themes, and a 6am shift at the dock is exactly when this one gets used.

c-edge.note: CONSOLE. Row hairline. Decorative, as in light.

c-accent.note: CONSOLE. Still a fill — but at 8.52:1 on c-bg it is legible as ink here too. The light theme is the stricter one, so the fill-only rule holds everywhere.

c-focus.note: CONSOLE. = the Night Dive focus ring — 11.11:1 on c-bg. On a dark ground the brand value already clears it, so there is no reason to diverge.

gradient.$note: Named washes from the board. Full stop lists and angles, verbatim.

seascape.note: the CSS stand-in for a sea photo: sky, horizon, water in one stack

seascape-desert.note: the CSS stand-in for a desert photo

photo-scrim.note: from the bottom edge wherever text overlays imagery

display.note: display, brand and every price. Round terminals that echo the line caps. Never below 19px, never a UI label. Variable 400..800.

ui.note: all UI and body — Latin, Cyrillic and Arabic in one family. Variable 300..600.

arabicDisplay.note: the rounded Arabic companion for display

console.note: CONSOLE · Daylight. All UI and body in the admin console and the operator app. Chosen over the mocked-up Public Sans because Plex carries latin, latin-ext AND cyrillic in one file — ru-RU is one of the seven locales, and Public Sans has no Cyrillic, so Russian would have fallen silently back to Rubik. Rubik stays in the stack as the last bundled resort. Variable 400..600.

consoleArabic.note: CONSOLE. The Arabic companion, same superfamily and same skeleton. The operator app is Arabic-first, so this is a primary face there, not a fallback. Variable 400..600.

figure.value: "IBM Plex Mono", "IBM Plex Sans Arabic", ui-monospace, monospace
figure.note: CONSOLE. Money, counts, references and ledger ids — a column of figures has to read down its own edge. Latin subset only at one weight: Arabic locales render Western digits, which the latin subset covers, and there is no bold figure in this design. Plex Sans Arabic sits second in the stack because figure slots are not only digits: a currency renders as ج.م. in Arabic, and a meter reads خلصت من 15 يوم. Plex Mono has no Arabic, so without it those letters fell through to the system monospace face, which sets Arabic one letter at a time with gaps between — unreadable, and only in the Arabic console.

mono.note: the system mono stack. The board uses ui-monospace for token names, focal-point read-outs and IDs. There is no bundled mono face.

weight.$note: Baloo 2 sets display at 600. Rubik carries UI: 300 / 400 / 500, and 500 is the heaviest UI weight.

displayXL.note: hero titles, max 2 lines. Tracking is positive.

caption.note: legal and FX disclosure, in text-muted

cTitle.note: CONSOLE · the screen title in the header. Negative tracking, unlike the traveller display roles — this is a grotesque, not Baloo.

cHeading.note: CONSOLE · panel heading, the name on a detail page.

cBody.note: CONSOLE · every row, every cell, every sentence.

cLabel.note: CONSOLE · the emphasised half of a row — an operator's name, a document's type.

cMeta.note: CONSOLE · the quiet second line under a label. Arabic lifts this to 15px through the +20% rule, which is why nothing smaller exists.

cOverline.note: CONSOLE · section eyebrow. Never a sentence, never Arabic-uppercased — Arabic has no case, so the transform is a no-op there by design.

cFigure.note: CONSOLE · the number on a stat tile, a total, a payout.

cFigureSm.note: CONSOLE · figures inside a row or a table cell, and ledger references.

cTab.note: CONSOLE · the label under a tab-bar icon. Smaller than cMeta because five tabs share a 375px phone — 75px per slot, and 'Operators' has to fit without truncating. The only role in the console allowed below 12px, and it is never a sentence.

cBadge.note: CONSOLE · the count riding on a tab or a rail entry. Digits only — never a word, which is why it may sit below the Arabic body minimum.

arabic.$note: Arabic gets +20% line-height (multiplier 1.2) and never sets below 15px.

wordmark.$note: DAHAB in display 600 at +0.01em (positive — it sits open). 'focal' at 0.22 of the DAHAB cap height, +0.2em tracking, in clay-500.

c-xs.note: CONSOLE · chips, pills on a dense row, the inner corner of a meter.

c-sm.note: CONSOLE · the default. Buttons, inputs, panels, cards. The traveller system's softest corner is 8px and its cards are 26px; the console is crisper on purpose, because a rounded box reads as an object and a dense screen is mostly not objects.

c-md.note: CONSOLE · a panel that genuinely is a separate object — a detail header, a stat tile.

c-lg.note: CONSOLE · bottom sheets, only where the sheet meets the screen edge.

shadow.$note: Prefer a tinted surface over a shadow. Shadows exist for lift only, and are warm-tinted (ink-900 at low alpha), never neutral grey.

confetti.note: booking success, from the bottom edge, once

signature.$note: sheet rise overshoots 6px; card lift is 4px; loading is a jellyfish mark drifting up through a mint wash; pull-to-refresh is a wave that crests at 60px and breaks on release. Every signature collapses to a 120ms opacity fade under prefers-reduced-motion.

texture.$note: paper grain at 0.04 opacity, multiply blend, on cream surfaces, never over text. Caustic shimmer at 0.06 opacity on mint washes only, 14s drift.

a11y.$note: WCAG 2.2 AA is a build gate. Ratios recomputed from the hexes in this file.

locale.$note: en-GB source; ar-EG is the only RTL. Western digits by default (Egyptian norm); Eastern is a settings toggle. Design for +40% label width — nothing truncates. Expansion factors: de 1.35, es 1.25, ru 1.20, fr 1.20, it 1.15, ar 0.75.

icon.$note: 37 marks on a 100-unit grid, 3px ink-line over a filled pastel silhouette offset +4/+4, six strokes or fewer. Purely abstract marks (sea, wind, weave, reef, depth, coral-fan) carry no silhouette. spark and tick are the two UI glyphs. The illustration set is the same hand, larger.

noFlip.$note: CLAUDE.md rule: icons of physical objects and media transport controls carry noFlip; everything else mirrors in RTL. The explicit per-icon list is not published on the board — this is a first pass and needs design sign-off (see docs/FOUNDATION.md).
